title: No racism in teen's death, officer says
subtitle: Duane Christian's skin colour played no role "whatsoever" in the teen's shooting death by a Toronto police officer, the officer told a coroner's inquest Wednesday. "The actions of the driver dictated my reaction," said Const. Steve Darnley.
article: Duane Christian's skin colour played no role "whatsoever" in the teen's shooting death by a Toronto police officer, the officer told a coroner's inquest Wednesday. "The actions of the driver dictated my reaction," said Const. Steve Darnley.

Darnley shot Christian, 15, in the arm and chest, through a passenger window, as the boy sat in the driver's seat of a stolen van in the parking lot of a Scarborough highrise apartment building shortly before 5 a.m. on June 20, 2006.
Darnley previously testified he had no other choice but to shoot the driver, who he believed was going to run over his partner to escape.

The province's Special Investigations Unit, a civilian agency that examines any incident involving police that results in serious injury or death, cleared Darnley of any wrongdoing two months after the incident, saying the officer was "legally justified" to shoot Christian "to prevent his partner from being deliberately run down."
Christian's family, however, has launched a landmark $2 million negligence lawsuit against the SIU.

In his second day of testimony, Darnley, 36, said the older model Dodge Caravan Christian was driving is a frequent target of theft, so he and his partner wanted to verify its licence plate. Because of the van's tinted windows, he didn't know the driver's age or race. They followed the van into a parking lot and determined it was stolen. Darnley said he drew his gun because stolen vehicles are often connected to violent crimes.
When a juror asked Darnley why he hadn't simply told his partner to get out of the way, Darnley said the situation was "dynamic" and there wasn't enough time. No weapon was found on Christian's body.
